description: Approved differences between gtfs.guru and MobilityData/gtfs-validator on the pinned real-world corpus. An entry documents a difference the project has decided to accept or has not triaged yet; anything not listed here is a parity regression. Totals are pinned, so a difference that changes size loses its approval and resurfaces. Use "absent" when a validator does not emit the code at all, and omit a total to accept any value. See docs/real-world-parity.md.

entries.reason: Triaged 2026-09-15 (GTF-34). stop_times.txt rows 130-135 have pickup_type=2 and drop_off_type=2 with pickup/drop-off windows and no booking rule ids: 6 rows x 2 fields = 12, and the Java rule has the same semantics. Java reports nothing because booking_rules.txt row 7 carries an invalid_url, its loader marks that table UNPARSABLE_ROWS, and every validator injecting the booking rules table is skipped for the whole feed. gtfs.guru does not skip validators on field parse errors. Kept: these are genuine defects Java under-reports.

Triaged 2026-09-15 (GTF-34). The extra occurrence is booking_rules.txt row 7 (booking_rule_000006): booking_type=1 and an empty prior_notice_duration_min, exactly like the eleven rows both validators report. Java drops the row before validation because its info_url fails to parse (the feed's single invalid_url, reported by both validators), so BookingRulesEntityValidator never sees it. gtfs.guru keeps rows with field-level parse errors. Kept: the notice is correct on the data.

Triaged 2026-09-15 (GTF-34). calendar.txt rows 12, 25, 29, 41 and 43 (service_ids 17, 47, 53, 340, 343) have every weekday set to 0 and no calendar_dates.txt additions, so the services never run. service_never_active has no canonical equivalent and is already an acknowledged addition in spec_baseline.json and spec_changes.json. Kept.
